Summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Redwood walked Pinegrove through rate limiting and multi-tenant controls in the Console and API. Focus on org/project keys, per-project quotas, and dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs. Security questions around SSO, KMS and audit logs. Agreement to share pricing and security docs and schedule a technical VPC deep-dive.

Topics: rate limits, org/project keys, quotas, RBAC, VPC/private deployment, SOC2/KMS, Dedicated capacity, throughput benchmarks

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone? thanks for joining, i'm alex from redwood. can you see my screen?
[00:06] Maya: yep seeing it, thanks alex.
[00:08] Ethan: looks good. we have about 40 minutes — want to focus on rate limiting, org and project keys, and how we isolate tenants.
[00:15] Alex: perfect. i'll do a short walkthrough of the console then jump into the API and sample configs. samira will cover the VPC/dedicated bits. quick qual — maya, can you remind me of your deployment targets? hosted API or private?
[00:29] Maya: we're piloting hosted but need the option for private/vpc for PHI. timeline is q1 production for samples, bigger rollout later.
[00:38] Alex: got it. and current traffic patterns?
[00:41] Ethan: average 120 rps, spikes to about 900 during our batch processing windows; token usage roughly 400k tokens per day across a few endpoints.
[00:52] Samira: ok that's helpful. in the console i'll show org-level controls first — you can set org-wide quotas, then project-keys for each product. those keys have per-second rate-limits, monthly usage quotas, and role-scoped permissions.
[01:05] Alex: quick note — our project keys are intended for multi-tenant setups; you can create one key per product, and then apply per-key policies so if one customer spikes it doesn't take down others.
[01:14] Lena: how do you map keys to our internal tenant ids? we need auditability and SSO mapping.
[01:20] Samira: you can attach metadata to keys (customer id, team, environment). that shows up in audit logs. SSO/SAML can provision user accounts and RBAC maps to console actions. audit events include key creation, key rotation, rate-limit enforcement events.
[01:35] Maya: are enforcement events shipped to our SIEM?
[01:37] Samira: yes, logs can be pushed to your logging endpoint or stored in customer-managed S3 for Private; we also support webhook alerts for enforcement triggers.
[01:45] Ethan: on the enforcement itself — is throttling token-based or request-based? i.e., per-token cost accounting vs rps.
[01:52] Alex: both. rate-limits are request-based (requests per second) but quotas can be token-based monthly caps. for example you can limit a project key to 50 rps and 1M tokens per month.
[02:05] Maya: what about burst behaviour? our spikes are short but big.
[02:09] Samira: we have a configurable burst bucket. for Dedicated customers you can request higher burst limits, and we do graceful degradation — fallback to a cheaper model variant or queue requests based on policy.
[02:21] Ethan: that sounds good. latency is critical on some endpoints; would fallback affect latency a lot?
[02:26] Alex: yes there's a tradeoff. fallback to a quantized variant could slightly increase error rate or change quality; but it keeps latency bounded. we can also route critical traffic to Dedicated pools pinned to higher perf GPUs.
[02:38] Lena: on compliance — we're regulated. SOC2 is a must, plus KMS-backed encryption, rotation policies. how does redwood handle key management for Private vs Hosted?
[02:48] Samira: for Hosted we offer BYOK via cloud KMS integrations; for Private you can bring your own HSM. rotation policies are configurable and audit-logged. we also provide field-level access controls and isolation of logs per org.
[02:59] Maya: do you support customer-managed VPC peering?
[03:02] Samira: yes, we have VPC peering and Private link options, and a network checklist we can share. for air-gapped on-prem we ship an appliance.
[03:10] Ethan: back to rate limits — can we have both org-wide and project-specific policies, and precedence rules?
[03:15] Alex: yes, precedence: per-key policy overrides project defaults which override org defaults. you can also set fallback policies — e.g., when a project exceeds its token quota, block; or degrade to read-only, or route to a cheaper model.
[03:30] Maya: are there SDK hooks to expose rate-limit headers to our clients? we want the frontend to get a retry-after header.
[03:36] Alex: we emit standard headers X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After. SDKs in our node/python libs expose helpers for retry/backoff.
[03:45] Ethan: can we do dynamic per-tenant weights? some tenants pay more and should have higher limits.
[03:50] Samira: yep, we support weighted limits and billing tiers. you can attach billing plans to projects and keys.
[03:57] Alex: i'll demo the console quickly — bear with me if the demo is a bit laggy.
[04:02] [Screen share: Redwood Console - Org settings page; Samira navigating]
[04:15] Samira: here you can see org quotas, top usage graphs, and project list. click into a project — you'll see keys, per-key quotas and attachments.
[04:28] [Mouse clicks. Slight audio overlap.]
[04:32] Samira: creating a key — give it a name, attach metadata, set rps limit, token quota per month, and link to billing plan. rotation is one-click.
[04:45] Maya: can we set quotas per environment (prod/staging)?
[04:48] Samira: yes, keys can be scoped to env tags. also you can auto-revoke keys in staging on schedule.
[04:56] Ethan: what's the enforcement granularity? continent, region, or global?
[04:59] Alex: enforcement is global by default but can be regionally scoped if you route traffic to regional endpoints. that helps with data residency concerns.
[05:09] Lena: about logs — can we get per-tenant usage reports for billing reconciliation?
[05:13] Samira: daily usage exports per project/key. we also offer streaming exports for high-fidelity billing.
[05:20] Maya: competition question — how's this different from Anthropic/OpenAI offerings?
[05:25] Alex: primary difference is the production controls: org/project keys, per-key policies, built-in routing and fallback policies, and Dedicated pools you can reserve. also better observability per token.
[05:36] Ethan: performance question — do you do KV cache sharing across tenants? we need cache isolation for security.
[05:41] Samira: caches are per-model instance and we isolate tenant caches for multi-tenant hosts. Dedicated pools can be single-tenant to avoid any sharing.
[05:50] Maya: ok can you show an example API request with org and project key?
[05:54] Alex: sure. example curl: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer project_key_xxx" -H "X-Org: pinegrove" post /v1/generate {"model":"redwood-large","input":"..."} the project_key carries the policy.
[06:07] Ethan: do you version keys or rotate automatically?
[06:10] Alex: you can enable auto-rotation and shadow keys for zero-downtime rotation. all rotation events are logged.
[06:18] Maya: question on tenant isolation in logs — PII redaction?
[06:22] Samira: yes, we support automated PII redaction for hosted logs and options to redact before exporting. for Private you control that pipeline.
[06:32] Ethan: what about enforcement latency — how quickly do rate limit configs propagate?
[06:36] Alex: usually within seconds; when you push a policy it's distributed to edge routers and enforcement is near real-time.
[06:44] Lena: one more compliance question — do you provide signed artifacts for audits?
[06:48] Samira: yes, we can provide signed audit logs, evidence packages, and support for your external audits.
[06:55] Maya: ok this is helpful. two quick scenarios: 1) we want per-customer soft limits with alerts, and 2) for premium customers hard limits that trigger billing upgrades. how would you model that?
[07:06] Alex: model 1: set project key with soft quota (alert threshold at 80%) and webhook -> internal alerting. model 2: tiered billing + per-key hard cap that denies requests beyond quota. we can also automate upgrade flows via API.
[07:20] Ethan: any examples of large customers doing auto-escalation?
[07:24] Alex: yes we have a case with a marketplace customer who auto-promoted tenants when usage hit 90% and routed overflow to a burst dedicated pool. we'll share that notes doc.
[07:34] Maya: about Dedicated — cost and SLA?
[07:36] Samira: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools, monthly commit, with SLA for throughput and latency. pricing depends on commit size and GPU class; i'll include a tiered price sheet.
[07:46] Ethan: do you support quantized model variants for lower-cost fallbacks?
[07:49] Alex: yes, Optimize suggests quantization and we can create model variants. the runtime handles kernel selection and KV cache so switching is sane.
[07:58] [Small silence — typing]
[08:02] Maya: for the technical deep-dive can samira's team work with our infra folks about VPC peering and throughput tests?
[08:08] Alex: absolutely, let's set that up. samira, you'll lead?
[08:11] Samira: yes. i'll prepare a checklist and sample k8s/network config and we'll schedule a one-hour bench next week.
[08:18] Ethan: timeline for security docs? we need SOC2 asap.
[08:21] Samira: i'll share SOC2, encryption, KMS, and audit log docs after the call.
[08:26] Maya: ai model behavior — do you provide eval tooling tied to rollouts so we can catch regressions?
[08:30] Alex: yes, Redwood Optimize includes eval sets and regression alerts; you can tie alerts to rollouts and auto-roll-back policies.
[08:38] Lena: last security nit — encryption in transit and at rest, is there any customer-managed key where you don't have plaintext access?
[08:44] Samira: with BYOK and HSMs we don't have access. all decryption happens in your environment for private deployments.
[08:52] Maya: great. let's recap.
[08:54] Alex: recap: 1) Alex will send pricing + dedicated tiers; 2) Samira to share SOC2/security docs and VPC/network checklist; 3) schedule technical deep-dive with Ethan and infra; 4) Ethan to send RPS and token patterns. agreed?
[09:08] Maya: yes. one more — can you include sample rate-limit policies we can review?
[09:12] Alex: yes will include examples: soft/hard, burst config, failover to cheaper model.
[09:18] Ethan: thanks all.
[09:20] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up by end of week.

[End of recording]
